hero.eyebrow: Thinking skills · No software to install
hero.title: Critical Thinking: weigh claims, decide well, solve problems
hero.subtitle: Sort facts from assumptions, map arguments in a document editor and score decisions in a working spreadsheet. Every task is checked and explained.
hero.outcomeLine: After this course you can examine arguments, avoid common traps and solve problems systematically.

outcomes.title: Think fairly
outcomes.text: Facts, opinions, assumptions and good questions.

outcomes.title: Spot fallacies and biases
outcomes.text: Name the error and counter it.

outcomes.title: Check what you read
outcomes.text: Evaluate news and claims before sharing.

projects.title: A case analysis
projects.text: Problem, causes, options and a tested recommendation.

tools.title: Spreadsheet lab
tools.text: For decision matrices and Pareto tables.

assessment: Finish the required labs in each module: they are checked automatically and explained when something is missing.
Pass each module quiz (70% or more). You can retry as often as you like.
Complete the case analysis and the final assessment.

faq.a: No. It is a practical course on reasoning, deciding and solving problems in study and work.
Only basic arithmetic. The spreadsheet labs use simple formulas and the course explains them.

faq.q: Will this make me argue with everyone?
faq.a: Hopefully not! The aim is to think fairly and persuade with evidence, not to win arguments.

activities.title: Map an argument
activities.objective: Set out a claim with reasons, evidence and a counter-argument.
activities.scenario: A student council wants to argue that the library should stay open until 10 pm. Write it as a short structured argument.
steps: Add Heading 2 sections: Claim, Reasons, Evidence, Objection and reply.
State the claim in one sentence.
List at least three reasons in a bulleted list.
Give at least one piece of evidence with a number.
State one objection and reply to it.

checks.label: Four sections
checks.hint: Use Heading 2 for each section.
checks.explain: Structure shows how the argument fits together.

checks.label: Sections in order
checks.hint: Claim, Reasons, Evidence, Objection and reply.
checks.explain: From conclusion to support to challenge.

checks.label: Three reasons
checks.hint: Use the bullet button.
checks.explain: Several independent reasons make a claim stronger.

checks.label: Evidence with a number
checks.hint: Include a figure or survey result.

checks.label: An objection and a reply
checks.hint: Write 'Some people say...' and a response.
checks.explain: Good arguments face the best counter-view.

checks.label: Between 110 and 280 words
checks.hint: Concise.
checks.explain: A short argument is easier to check.

activities.title: Weighted decision matrix
activities.objective: Compare options fairly by scoring them against weighted criteria.
activities.scenario: A student is choosing between three laptops. Score each against four criteria and weight what matters most.
steps: In E2 total the weighted score for Laptop A: multiply each score by its weight in row 7 (lock the weights with dollar signs) and add the three results.
Fill the same pattern for rows 3 and 4.
In B9 find the highest score with MAX.
In B10 name the winner with IF.

checks.label: E2 is Laptop A's weighted score
checks.explain: Multiply each score by its weight and add.

checks.label: E3 is Laptop B's score
checks.hint: Same pattern in row 3.
checks.explain: Locking the weights keeps them fixed.

checks.label: E4 is Laptop C's score
checks.hint: Same pattern in row 4.
checks.explain: Compare all options on the same scale.

checks.label: B9 is the highest score
checks.hint: =MAX(E2:E4)

checks.label: B10 names the winner
checks.explain: Match the top score to its option.

activities.title: Five whys
activities.objective: Ask why repeatedly to move from symptom to root cause.
activities.scenario: A website checkout page lost half its customers last week. Use the five whys to find the cause.
steps: Write a first line starting with Problem:.
Write five numbered lines each starting with Why.
End with a line starting Root cause: and a line starting Fix:.

checks.label: A problem line
checks.hint: Start with Problem:.

checks.label: Five whys in a numbered list
checks.hint: Use the numbered list button for five lines.
checks.explain: Each answer becomes the next question.

checks.label: A root cause line
checks.hint: Add Root cause:.

checks.label: A fix line
checks.hint: Add Fix:.
checks.explain: A cause leads to an action.

checks.label: In a sensible order
checks.hint: Problem, then the whys, then Root cause, then Fix.

activities.title: Find the vital few with a Pareto chart
activities.objective: Rank causes by count and find the few that cause most of the problem.
activities.scenario: A help desk logged 500 complaints by cause. Find which causes make up most of them.
steps: In C2 enter the share of complaints: count divided by the total in B8 (lock B8).
Sort or arrange from the biggest cause downward (already sorted).
In D2 enter the cumulative share: =C2 and in D3 =D2+C3, filling down.
In B9 find the first cause where the cumulative share reaches 80% (just read it) by counting causes with cumulative below 0.8 using COUNTIF and adding 1.

checks.label: C2 is the first share
C7 is the last share
checks.hint: Fill down.

checks.label: D2 starts the cumulative share
checks.hint: Type =C2 here, then add each later share to the running total.
checks.explain: The first cumulative equals the first share.

checks.label: D4 is cumulative to the third cause
checks.explain: Add each share to the running total.

checks.label: D7 reaches 100%
checks.hint: Fill down.

checks.label: B9 counts causes to reach 80%
checks.explain: Count the rows still under 0.8 and add one.

activities.title: Final project: solve a case
activities.objective: Define a problem, find its cause, weigh options and recommend a solution with evidence.
activities.scenario: A small bakery's weekend sales have dropped 20% over two months while weekdays are steady. Write your analysis.
steps: Add a Heading 1 'Case analysis'.
Add Heading 2 sections: Problem, Possible causes, Evidence needed, Options, Recommendation.
Under Possible causes list at least three.
Under Options list at least two, each with a pro and a con.
Under Recommendation state the choice, a test and how you will measure success with a number.
Keep it between 150 and 340 words.

checks.label: A title
checks.hint: Use Heading 1.

checks.label: Five sections
checks.hint: Use Heading 2.

checks.label: Sections in order
checks.hint: Problem, Possible causes, Evidence needed, Options, Recommendation.

checks.label: At least three causes
checks.hint: Use the bullet button.

checks.label: Pros and cons appear
checks.hint: Use the words pro and con or advantage and risk.

checks.label: A measurable target
checks.hint: Include a number such as 10% in the recommendation.
checks.explain: Measure to know if it worked.

checks.label: Between 150 and 340 words
checks.hint: Concise.
